name: Thermoregulatory-Style Affect Regulation Circuit
short_description: Integrates affective state, affective setpoint, and environmental valence using thermoregulatory-style homeostatic regulation to select appropriate affect regulation strategies.

components.name: AFFECT_SENSOR
components.description: Monitors current affective state across valence and arousal dimensions

components.name: AFFECT_SETPOINT_COMPARATOR
components.description: Compares current affect to desired/comfortable affective state

components.name: ENVIRONMENTAL_VALENCE_ASSESSOR
components.description: Evaluates affective tone and availability of emotion regulation resources in environment

components.name: REGULATION_SELECTOR
components.description: Selects affect regulation strategy based on discrepancy and environmental affective resources

key_references: IJzerman, H., Coan, J. A., Wagemans, F. M., Missler, M. A., Beall, A. T., Ferro, K., ... & Vingerhoets, A. J. (2015). Social thermoregulation in the brain: Evidence from functional neuroimaging and behavioral studies. Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience, 10(8), 1110–1117.
Inagaki, T. K., & Eisenberger, N. I. (2013). Shared neural mechanisms underlying social warmth and physical warmth. Psychological Science, 24(11), 2272–2280.
design_implications: Social and physical warmth are affectively intertwined; design spaces that combine thermal comfort with social connection (e.g., gathering spaces with warm lighting and seating arrangements)
Environmental emotional tone (friendly, tense, calm) influences regulation; curate affective context through color, sound, and social cues to support desired affective states
